evals.prompt: My Go tests fail with compile errors referencing a generated package. What's the right debug sequence and which commands do I run?
evals.expected_behavior: Follows the documented debugging sequence: fix the generated-package compile error before anything else, then isolate the specific failing test rather than re-running the whole suite.
assertions: Runs `make generate` before retrying the test, since the failure is a compile error in a generated package
After generation is fixed, isolates with `go test -v -run TestName ./path/to/pkg` rather than jumping straight to the full suite
Presents the steps in the documented order (generate first, then isolate)
deterministic_checks: `make generate` runs before the test is retried
uses `go test -v -run TestName ./pkg/...` to isolate the failing test

evals.prompt: One test in the repository package is failing. Diagnose it.
evals.expected_behavior: Isolates and fixes the single failing test first with a narrow, verbose run, and only broadens to the full test target once that fix is confirmed.
assertions: Runs the narrow failing test with `go test -v -run TestName ./path/to/pkg` before touching anything else
Does not immediately run `make test` (the full suite) before the isolated fix is confirmed
Re-runs the narrow test after the fix, then broadens to the repository's test target only afterward
deterministic_checks: runs `go test -v -run TestName` scoped to the failing package before any full-suite command

evals.prompt: I added a new repository method for the orders feature. Make sure my test coverage is appropriate before I open a PR.
evals.expected_behavior: Confirms persistence-behavior coverage against a real or in-memory DB, keeps optional-DB tests skipping (not failing) when unavailable, and re-runs the broader test target before declaring the change ready.
assertions: Confirms repository-layer tests exercise persistence behavior against at least one real or in-memory DB
States that tests for an optional/unavailable DB should skip rather than fail
Confirms the broader test target (e.g. `make test`) is run before claiming the change is ready
States new features require tests before merge

evals.prompt: An integration test is failing with a database connection error. What should I check?
evals.expected_behavior: Follows the documented DB-related failure step: verifies DATABASE_URL is set and migrations are applied before assuming a code defect.
assertions: Checks whether migrations have been applied
Does not propose a code fix before ruling out DB setup issues

evals.prompt: The Go build fails with a toolchain version mismatch error, not a test failure — help me fix it.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes this is a build/toolchain problem rather than a test-debugging task and routes to go-build-and-test instead of applying the testing-workflows debugging sequence.
assertions: Does not apply the test-failure debugging sequence (generate/isolate/DB checks) to a toolchain mismatch
States this belongs to go-build-and-test rather than testing-workflows
Does not fabricate a test command to run for a build-only failure

evals.prompt: All the domain and repository tests pass now. Review the overall diff and tell me if it's ready to merge.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes the testing work is done and the remaining ask is a merge-readiness review, routing to implementation-review rather than continuing the test-debugging workflow.
assertions: Does not re-run the debugging sequence when tests already pass and the ask is about merge readiness
States this is a job for implementation-review, not testing-workflows
Does not fabricate a review verdict itself in place of the review skill
